assertions.assert: It diarizes the utterance through the speech service's `diarize` (`POST {base}/audio/diarization`, model `pyannote-diarization` by default); its `bot.ability.hearing.voice.diarization.output` is answered to its parent as `bot.ability.hearing.voice.diarization.output` exactly `{id, segments}`: one clipped PCM segment per answered span, ascending by start, each `{audio: "<output>-<index>", media_type: "audio/pcm", sample_rate_hz, channels, start_seconds, end_seconds, confidence}` (`confidence` `null` when the answer has none); raw speaker labels never enter. It is long-lived: each utterance is a request `bot.ability.hearing.voice.diarization.input` `{id, audio, media_type?, sample_rate_hz?, channels?, output}`.
The utterance is a WAV container (its own format) or raw 16-bit PCM in the request's `sample_rate_hz` and `channels`; raw PCM with no format is a failure.

When the service answers `bot.ability.failed` `{message}` (an error status, an answer with no spans, a span outside the utterance, a format it cannot read), it answers `bot.ability.failed` exactly `{id, message}`.
When the diarizer cannot run (a malformed `model` rejects its start with `error.execution`), it answers `bot.ability.failed` `{id, message: "VoiceDiarization could not run (<error event>)"}`.
